utterance: Hi Mark, I'm the GP today. Could you tell me when this started and how the cough and fever have changed since then?
reply: It started three days ago. The cough was dry and hacking at first. Then I started burning up, on and off. I didn’t have a thermometer, but I was definitely roasting.

utterance: Are you bringing up any phlegm or blood? Have you had trouble breathing or any pain in your chest?
reply: Yes, I’ve been bringing stuff up since yesterday, it’s a rusty, brownish colour, clear at first. No actual blood, just that rusty colour. I only got puffed going up the stairs, but I’m alright sitting here. There’s a sharp pain low down on the right side, near my back, it catches me when I take a deep breath or cough. It started yesterday.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Coughing up blood
Chest pain with breathing or coughing

utterance: Have you had shaking chills, faintness, confusion, or difficulty keeping fluids down? Are you passing urine normally?
reply: Yes, the first night I was shaking under the doona, teeth chattering, even though I was boiling. My head’s clear, though my wife reckons I’m just grumpy. I’ve been able to keep fluids down, and I’m passing urine normally.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Confusion or drowsiness

utterance: Have you had a runny nose, sore throat, headache, muscle aches or diarrhoea? Have you been around anyone unwell, or tested for COVID?
reply: No, I haven’t had a runny nose, sore throat, headache, muscle aches or diarrhoea. I haven’t been around anyone unwell, and I haven’t tested for COVID.

utterance: Have you had any recent travel, hospital stays, operations or long periods sitting still? Any swelling or pain in one leg, or history of blood clots?
reply: No, I haven’t had any recent travel, hospital stays or operations. I’ve just been going to school and home. Legs are fine, no swelling or pain in either one. No history of blood clots either.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Recent hospital stay
Red flag excluded: Leg swelling or calf pain

utterance: Do you have any past problems with your lungs, heart, kidneys, diabetes or your immune system? What medicines, supplements or treatments have you taken for this, and do you have any medicine allergies?
reply: No heart problems, no diabetes, no lung issues like asthma, no immune problems either. I haven’t had any antibiotics, but I had an allergy to penicillin when I was a kid – hives and swollen lips – it’s probably not on my file because I haven’t needed them in years.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Immune problems or immunosuppressant medicines

utterance: Thanks for telling me—that allergy is important. Did the swelling and hives come on soon after the penicillin, and did you have breathing problems or need emergency treatment? Are you taking anything else, including paracetamol or ibuprofen, and have you ever had kidney problems?
reply: The swelling and hives came on straight away after the penicillin. I didn’t have breathing problems, and I didn’t need emergency treatment. I’ve been taking paracetamol on and off for the fever. No, I’ve never had kidney problems.

finding: Normal chest shape. Breathing slightly fast; holds back on deep breaths on the right.
Expansion reduced on the right lower chest.
Lungs (front): Resonant. Lungs (back): Dull to percussion at the right base. Left base resonant. Elsewhere: dull at the right base posteriorly. Resonant elsewhere.

Lungs (front): Vesicular breath sounds. No added sounds. Lungs (back): Bronchial breathing with coarse crackles at the right base. Left base clear. Elsewhere: bronchial breathing and coarse crackles at the right base posteriorly. Vesicular elsewhere. No wheeze.
Lungs (front): Normal and symmetrical. Lungs (back): Increased at the right base. Elsewhere: increased at the right base posteriorly. Normal elsewhere.
Heart sounds dual, no added sounds. No murmurs.

utterance: Do you smoke or vape, and how much alcohol do you usually drink? Have you had pneumonia before?
reply: No, I’ve never smoked or vaped. I had a couple of beers on the weekend, but none this week. I haven’t had pneumonia before.

utterance: Your symptoms and the sounds at the bottom of your right lung suggest pneumonia, an infection in the lung. Your oxygen level and blood pressure are reassuring, and you appear well enough to treat at home if you have support. I'd like a chest X-ray today to confirm this and check for fluid around the lung. Is someone available to help you at home, and can you get to an X-ray and return for review?
reply: Yes, my wife is working from home this week, so she can drive me back if I need. I can get to an X-ray and return for review.

awards.label: Who is at home with him

result: Right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms. Other lobes clear. No pleural effusion. Normal heart size.

utterance: The X-ray confirms pneumonia in the lower part of your right lung, without a collection of fluid around it. You need an antibiotic. Because your childhood reaction suggests an immediate penicillin allergy, I will avoid penicillin and use doxycycline instead. Have you ever reacted to doxycycline or similar antibiotics, and are you taking any regular medicines, vitamins or antacids?
reply: No, I’ve never taken doxycycline or reacted to it. I’m on a low-dose blood pressure tablet and a vitamin B complex. No antacids.

utterance: What is the name and dose of your blood pressure tablet? Are there any other medicines you've taken recently?
reply: My blood pressure tablet is amlodipine 5mg. I haven’t taken anything else recently.

awards.label: Doxycycline 100 mg orally 12-hourly for 5–7 days (penicillin allergy)

utterance: Take one doxycycline tablet twice a day for five days, starting today. Take it with food and a full glass of water, sitting or standing, and don't lie down for at least 30 minutes afterwards or take it just before bed. Keep antacids and supplements containing iron, calcium, magnesium or zinc at least two hours away from it. It can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, so cover up and use sunscreen. If you develop hives or swelling, stop taking it and seek urgent help; call 000 if your lips or tongue swell or breathing becomes difficult. I'll note your penicillin allergy and your blood pressure medicine in your record.
reply: I'll take it as prescribed. Just wondering, do I need to do anything else before I go?

utterance: Rest at home, drink regularly, and stay off work while you have a fever or feel unwell. For fever or pain, you can take paracetamol 500 mg to 1 gram up to every six hours if needed, with no more than 4 grams in 24 hours; avoid doubling up with cold-and-flu medicines containing paracetamol. Please come back in 48 hours so we can check your breathing, oxygen level and response to treatment. You should start improving within two to three days, although the cough and tiredness can take several weeks to settle. If you aren't improving by then, or worsen at any point, don't wait for the appointment. Go to emergency urgently for increasing breathlessness, worsening chest pain, coughing up blood, persistent vomiting or inability to drink, or passing very little urine. Call 000 for severe trouble breathing, blue lips, collapse or confusion. If symptoms don't resolve we will reassess and may repeat your X-ray. Do you have any concerns about this plan?
reply: No, I don't have any concerns. Just hoping it kicks in and I can get back to teaching before the exams.

utterance: I understand—give yourself time to recover rather than pushing through. I can provide a medical certificate for school. We'll review you in two days, sooner if anything worsens. Once you're well we can also review your vaccinations and consider a specialist assessment of your penicillin allergy; don't try penicillin yourself.
reply: I didn’t get round to the flu jab this year.

utterance: Thanks for letting me know. Once your fever has settled and you're recovering, we can arrange your flu vaccination and check whether your COVID vaccinations are up to date. These help prevent future infections, but won't treat this pneumonia.
reply: No problem. I'll make sure to get that sorted once I'm feeling better.
